resource.name: aws_redshift_endpoint_authorization
resource.description: Creates a new Amazon Redshift endpoint authorization.
resource.llm_summary: The `aws_redshift_endpoint_authorization` resource enables the creation and management of endpoint authorizations for Amazon Redshift, allowing external accounts to access a Redshift-managed VPC endpoint. This resource is commonly used to facilitate secure cross-account data sharing, integrate Redshift clusters with third-party services, or grant access to analytics platforms. Users can configure permissions, account-level access controls, and lifecycle policies to streamline collaboration and ensure compliance with data-sharing requirements.

examples.llm_summary: This example demonstrates how to configure an AWS Redshift Endpoint Authorization using the `aws_redshift_endpoint_authorization` resource. It shows how to grant access to a specific AWS account (`account` argument) for a Redshift cluster identified by the `cluster_identifier` attribute, enabling cross-account access to the cluster.

arguments.name: account
arguments.description: (Required) The Amazon Web Services account ID to grant access to.
arguments.llm_summary: The `account` argument specifies the AWS account ID to which access is granted for using a Redshift-managed VPC endpoint, enabling cross-account connectivity. This required parameter allows users to define the recipient account for the authorization, facilitating secure data sharing and collaboration between AWS accounts.

arguments.name: cluster_identifier
arguments.description: (Required) The cluster identifier of the cluster to grant access to.
arguments.llm_summary: The `cluster_identifier` argument specifies the unique identifier of the Amazon Redshift cluster to which access is being granted through the `aws_redshift_endpoint_authorization` resource. By defining this required parameter, users enable external accounts to connect to the specified cluster, facilitating secure data sharing and cross-account access in Redshift environments.

arguments.name: force_delete
arguments.description: (Optional) Indicates whether to force the revoke action. If true, the Redshift-managed VPC endpoints associated with the endpoint authorization are also deleted. Default value is `false`.
arguments.llm_summary: The `force_delete` argument in the `aws_redshift_endpoint_authorization` resource allows users to control whether the revocation of an endpoint authorization also deletes associated Redshift-managed VPC endpoints. Setting this to `true` ensures a complete cleanup of dependent resources, aligning with user goals for resource lifecycle management and avoiding orphaned infrastructure.

arguments.name: id
arguments.llm_summary: The `id` argument in the `aws_redshift_endpoint_authorization` resource represents the unique identifier for the endpoint authorization, typically auto-generated or derived from the resource's attributes. While optional, it can be used to reference or manage the specific authorization instance, aiding in resource tracking or integration workflows.

arguments.name: vpc_ids
arguments.description: (Optional) The virtual private cloud (VPC) identifiers to grant access to. If none are specified all VPCs in shared account are allowed.
arguments.llm_summary: The `vpc_ids` argument in the `aws_redshift_endpoint_authorization` resource allows users to specify a set of VPC IDs that are granted access to the Redshift-managed endpoint. By defining this argument, users can control which specific VPCs in the shared account are authorized, enabling fine-grained access management; if omitted, all VPCs in the shared account are permitted by default.

attributes.name: allowed_all_vpcs
attributes.description: Indicates whether all VPCs in the grantee account are allowed access to the cluster.

attributes.name: endpoint_count
attributes.description: The number of Redshift-managed VPC endpoints created for the authorization.

attributes.name: grantee
attributes.description: The Amazon Web Services account ID of the grantee of the cluster.

attributes.name: grantor
attributes.description: The Amazon Web Services account ID of the cluster owner.
